lines.text: Your team ships with a pipeline of agents. But the whole thing is just a habit in people’s heads.
A new teammate has to ask around to learn the order, and nobody can point to one page.
Agent R Q Workflows turns that habit into a visual graph that everyone can read.
Each stage is a workspace. Build, review, test, and ship each get a node on the graph.
Events are the links between them. Build emits code changed, and that is the signal the next stage listens for.
Drag a workspace onto an event, and an event onto a workspace. The graph draws itself.
Then watch the pipeline run. Each event fires, and each workspace picks up its next task.
Save it as a named workflow, so everyone sees the same picture.
Now the team shares one picture. A new teammate opens it, and understands the order in a minute.
Each workspace keeps its approvals, so the pipeline never ships without a human saying yes.
And when the process changes, you change the graph. Add a stage, wire it up, and save.
Could you draw your team pipeline on one page? Tell us what is missing, and try Workflows at Agent R Q dot com.
